questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is not an example of heterogenous catalytic reaction?
questions.sol_text:
Combustion of coal does not use heterogeneous catalyst. Let's analyze each process:

Ostwald process: V2O5 (s) is used as a heterogeneous catalyst. The reactants (NH3 and O2) are gases, and the catalyst is solid.

Combustion of coal: This is a direct burning process that does not involve any catalyst. It is a spontaneous combustion reaction and does not use a heterogeneous catalyst.

Hydrogenation of vegetable oils: Ni (s) is used as a heterogeneous catalyst. The reactants (liquid oils and H2 gas) react on the surface of solid nickel catalyst.

Haber's process: Fe/Mo(s) is used as a heterogeneous catalyst. The reactants (N2 and H2 gases) are in different phase than the solid catalyst.

Therefore, combustion of coal is the only process that does not use a heterogeneous catalyst.

questions.text: Among the following, the INCORRECT statement about colloids is:
options: The range of diameters of colloidal particles is between 1 and to 1000 nm
they are larger than small molecules and have high molar mass
The osmotic pressure of a colloidal solution is of higher order than the true solution at the same concentration
questions.sol_text:
Osmotic pressure of colloidal solution is lower than true solution of same concentration.

Let us analyze each statement:

(1) The range of diameters of colloidal particles is between 1 and 1000 nm - CORRECT. This is the standard definition of colloidal particles.

(2) They are larger than small molecules and have high molar mass - CORRECT. Colloidal particles are much larger than small molecules and have high molar mass compared to molecular solutions.

(3) They can scatter light - CORRECT. This is the Tyndall effect, a characteristic property of colloids. Colloidal particles are large enough to scatter light.

(4) The osmotic pressure of a colloidal solution is of higher order than the true solution at the same concentration - INCORRECT. The osmotic pressure of a colloidal solution is LOWER than that of a true solution at the same concentration. This is because colloidal particles have a much larger size compared to molecules in a true solution. For the same mass concentration, the number of colloidal particles is much less than the number of solute molecules in a true solution. Since osmotic pressure depends on the number of particles (π = iMRT), the osmotic pressure of colloids is lower.

questions.text: Among the following the false statement is -

It is possible to cause artificial rain by throwing electrified sand carrying charge opposite to the one on clouds from an aeroplane
Latex is a colloidal solution of rubber particles which are positively charged
questions.sol_text:
Let us analyze each statement:

(1) Lyophilic sol can be coagulated by adding an electrolyte - TRUE
Lyophilic sols can be coagulated by adding an electrolyte, which decreases the dielectric constant of the medium and removes the solvation layer around colloidal particles.

(2) Tyndall effect can be used to distinguish between a colloidal solution and a true solution - TRUE
The Tyndall effect (scattering of light by colloidal particles) is observed in colloidal solutions but not in true solutions, making it a useful method to distinguish between them.

(3) It is possible to cause artificial rain by throwing electrified sand carrying charge opposite to the one on clouds from an aeroplane - TRUE
This is based on the principle of electrostatic precipitation. When oppositely charged particles are brought near clouds, they coagulate with cloud particles, leading to condensation and artificial rain.

(4) Latex is a colloidal solution of rubber particles which are positively charged - FALSE
Latex is indeed a colloidal solution of rubber particles, but these particles are NEGATIVELY charged, not positively charged. This is the false statement.

Therefore, the answer is [4].

questions.text: Tyndall effect is observed when-
options: The diameter of dispersed particles is similar to the wavelength of light used
the diameter of dispersed particles is much smaller than the wavelength of light used
The refractive index of dispersed phase is greater than that of the dispersion medium
The diameter of dispersed particles is much larger than the wavelength of light used
questions.sol_text:
The diameter of dispersed particles is similar to wavelength of light used.

The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles suspended in a fluid medium. This effect occurs when:

- The size of dispersed particles is comparable to (similar to) the wavelength of visible light being used
- When particle diameter ~ wavelength of light, significant light scattering occurs
- If particles are much smaller than wavelength (option 2), they don't scatter light effectively (very little Tyndall effect)
- If particles are much larger than wavelength (option 4), they cause ordinary reflection/refraction, not the characteristic Tyndall effect
- The refractive index difference (option 3) is a necessary condition but not the defining condition for observing Tyndall effect

Therefore, the Tyndall effect is characteristically observed when the particle diameter is similar to the wavelength of light used.

questions.text: An ionic micelle is formed on the addition of: excess water to liquid
options: N with H3C and CH3 groups attached to imidazole ring with PF6^- counterion, excess water to liquid
N with H3C and CH3 groups attached to imidazole ring with long alkyl chain and SO4^- counterion
liquid diethyl ether to aqueous NaCl solution
questions.sol_text:
Correct Ans. is (3)

An ionic micelle is formed when an ionic surfactant (amphiphilic molecule with both hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions) is added to an appropriate solvent. 

Analyzing each option:

(1) Ionic liquid (imidazolium PF6^-) + excess water: This forms a homogeneous ionic liquid solution, not a micelle, as the PF6^- anion is not sufficiently lipophilic to drive micelle formation in water.

(2) Sodium stearate + pure toluene: Sodium stearate is an anionic surfactant that forms micelles in aqueous media, not in nonpolar solvents like toluene. In toluene, the ionic surfactant would not aggregate into micelles.

(3) Imidazolium surfactant with long alkyl chain + SO4^- counterion + excess water: This is a typical cationic ionic surfactant. The long alkyl chain is hydrophobic while the imidazolium head group with SO4^- counterion is hydrophilic. Upon addition to water, the molecules self-assemble to form ionic micelles with the hydrophobic chains directed inward and the ionic heads directed outward in contact with water.

(4) Diethyl ether + aqueous NaCl solution: These are immiscible liquids that form separate phases; no micelle formation occurs.

Option (3) contains a proper ionic surfactant with both hydrophobic alkyl chain and hydrophilic ionic head group, which forms ionic micelles in water.

questions.text: A sample of red ink (a colloidal suspension) is prepared by mixing eosin dye, egg white, HCHO and water. The component which ensures stability of the ink sample is:
questions.sol_text:
In a colloidal suspension, stability is maintained by a protective colloid. Let's analyze each component:

(1) Eosin dye - This is the dispersed phase (colored component) that gives the ink its color. It does not provide stability.

(2) HCHO (Formaldehyde) - This acts as a preservative to prevent microbial growth, but does not provide colloidal stability.

(3) Water - This is the dispersion medium but does not prevent aggregation of colloidal particles.

(4) Egg white - Egg white is a protein (albumin) that acts as a protective colloid. Proteins adsorb on the surface of colloidal particles and form a protective layer around them. This prevents particle aggregation and flocculation, thereby ensuring the stability of the colloidal suspension.

The protein coating reduces interfacial tension and prevents the dispersed particles from coming together. This is why egg white is used as a stabilizing agent in the preparation of red ink.

Answer: (4) Egg white

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Identify the correct molecular picture showing that happens at the critical micellar concentration (CMC) of an aqueous solution of a surfactant (○ polar head; ~ non-polar tail; • water).
questions.sol_text:
At the critical micellar concentration (CMC), surfactant molecules begin to aggregate and form micelles in solution.

Before CMC: Surfactant molecules exist as individual monomers dispersed in water, with polar heads oriented towards the aqueous solution and non-polar tails avoiding water contact.

At CMC: The concentration reaches a point where surfactant molecules start to self-assemble into micelles. In an aqueous solution, these form as spherical structures with:
- Polar heads facing outward (in contact with the polar aqueous environment)
- Non-polar tails pointing inward (away from water, creating a hydrophobic core)

Analyzing the options:
(A) Shows individual surfactant molecules dispersed - this is below CMC
(B) Shows some aggregation beginning - intermediate stage
(C) Shows multiple micelles with proper spherical structure - this represents the state at CMC when micelles have formed
(D) Shows another configuration

Option (D) shows the characteristic spherical micelle structure where polar heads (circles) are oriented outward towards the water (dots) and non-polar tails (wavy lines) are directed inward. This is the correct representation of what occurs at the CMC.

questions.text: Adsorption of a gas follows Freundlich adsorption isotherm. If x is the mass of the gas adsorbed on mass m of the adsorbent, the correct of x/m versus p is -
options: Graph (1): Linear plots with 200 K, 250 K, 270 K curves increasing with p
Graph (2): Linear plots with 270 K, 250 K, 200 K curves (reversed order) increasing with p
Graph (3): Curved plots with 200 K, 250 K, 270 K curves showing concave pattern
Graph (4): Curved plots with 270 K, 250 K, 200 K curves (reversed order) showing concave pattern
questions.sol_text: The Freundlich adsorption isotherm is given by: x/m = K.P^(1/n), where x is mass of gas adsorbed, m is mass of adsorbent, P is pressure, K and n are constants. Taking logarithm: log(x/m) = log(K) + (1/n)log(P). This is a linear relationship between log(x/m) and log(P). However, when plotting x/m versus P (linear scale), the relationship is non-linear and follows a curve that is concave downward. The equation x/m = K.P^(1/n) shows that at constant pressure, as temperature increases, the adsorption decreases (K decreases with temperature). Therefore, at higher temperatures, the curves are lower. The correct graph should show: (1) Curved (non-linear) plots following Freundlich equation (2) Temperature order from bottom to top: 200 K, 250 K, 270 K (higher temperature = lower adsorption). Graph (3) matches both criteria: it shows curved plots with the correct temperature ordering where 200 K has maximum adsorption, followed by 250 K and 270 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: As per Hardy-Schulze formulation, the flocculation values of the following for ferric hydroxide sol are in the order:
questions.sol_text: According to Hardy-Schulze rule, coagulation value alpha = 1/(Coagulation Power). The coagulation power depends on the charge of the counter ion and its polarizing effect. For ferric hydroxide sol (positive colloid), anions are the counter ions. The order of coagulation power follows: Higher charge density and smaller size = higher coagulation power = lower coagulation value (flocculation value). K3[Fe(CN)6] has charge -3 (highest charge), K2CrO4 has charge -2, KBr and KNO3 have charge -1, and AlCl3 provides Al^(3+) cation with charge +3. Since ferric hydroxide is positively charged, the divalent and trivalent anions coagulate more effectively than monovalent ions. The order of flocculation values (coagulation values) is: K3[Fe(CN)6] < K2CrO4 < KBr = KNO3 = AlCl3. The trivalent anion K3[Fe(CN)6] has the highest coagulation power (lowest coagulation value), followed by divalent K2CrO4, then monovalent KBr and KNO3 with equal values, and AlCl3 is also among the least effective.

questions.text: A mixture of gases O2, H2 and CO are taken in a closed vessel containing charcoal. The graph that represents the correct behaviour of pressure with time is:
options: Pressure decreasing with time (curved, approaching zero)
questions.sol_text:
When a mixture of gases O2, H2 and CO are taken in a closed vessel containing charcoal, the charcoal will react with these gases through various reactions:

1. Charcoal reacts with O2: C + O2 → CO2
2. Charcoal reacts with H2: C + H2 → CH4 (or other hydrocarbons)
3. CO can react with charcoal under certain conditions

As these reactions proceed, the total number of moles of gas in the system decreases because:
- O2 is consumed (2 moles reactants → products)
- H2 is consumed
- The products formed may dissolve or condense

Since the vessel is closed and the volume is constant, by the ideal gas law (PV = nRT), as the number of moles (n) decreases while V and T remain constant, the pressure must decrease.

The pressure decreases gradually over time as the reactions continue. Initially, the pressure decreases rapidly when reactants are abundant, but as reactants get consumed, the reaction rate slows down. Eventually, the pressure approaches a constant value (or nearly constant) when the reaction essentially stops.

This behavior is best represented by option (4), which shows pressure decreasing with time in a curved manner (following first-order kinetics or similar) and eventually leveling off.

on increasing time, pressure will be decreases.

questions.text: The conditions given below are in the context of observing Tyndall effect in colloidal solutions: (a) The diameter of the colloidal particles is comparable to the wavelength of light used. (b) The diameter of the colloidal particles in much smaller than the wavelength of light used. (c) The diameter of the colloidal particles is much larger than the wavelength of light used. (d) The refractive indices of the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium are comparable. (e) The dispersed phase has a very different refractive index from the dispersion medium. Choose the most appropriate conditions from the options given below.
questions.sol_text: Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles. For Tyndall effect to occur: (1) The particle size should be comparable to the wavelength of light used (condition a) - particles much smaller (b) or much larger (c) than wavelength do not show Tyndall effect effectively. (2) The dispersed phase and dispersion medium must have significantly different refractive indices (condition e) - comparable refractive indices (condition d) would not scatter light effectively. Therefore, the correct conditions are (a) and (e).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Most suitable salt which can be used for efficient clotting of blood will be:
questions.sol_text: Blood is a negatively charged colloid. According to Hardy-Schulze Rule, for efficient coagulation of a negatively charged colloid, a cation with high positive charge and low size (high charge density) is needed. FeCl3 provides Fe3+ ions which have high positive charge (+3) and small ionic radius, making it most effective for blood clotting. The ferric ion can neutralize the negative charge on blood colloidal particles, causing rapid coagulation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In Freundlich adsorption isotherm, slope of AB line is:
questions.sol_text: Freundlich adsorption isotherm equation: x/m = kp^(1/n). Taking logarithm: log(x/m) = (1/n)log p + log k. Comparing with y = mx + C, the slope of the line AB is 1/n, where n is the Freundlich constant with values typically between 0 to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE for hydrophilic sols?
options: They do not require electrolytes for stability.
These sols are reversible in nature.
The sols cannot be easily coagulated.
Their viscosity is of the order of that of H2O.
questions.sol_text: Viscosity of the hydrophilic sol is always higher than H2O, because dispersed phase particles increase the viscosity of the dispersion medium. Therefore, statement (D) is FALSE. Hydrophilic sols do not require electrolytes for stability (A is TRUE), they are reversible in nature (B is TRUE), and they cannot be easily coagulated (C is TRUE).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In Freundlich adsorption isotherm at moderate pressure, the extent of adsorption (x/m) is directly proportional to P^x. The value of x is:
questions.sol_text: The Freundlich adsorption isotherm is given by (x/m) = k(P)^n. At moderate pressure, x/m varies non-linearly with P. From the equation (x/m) = k(P)^n, we can see that (x/m) is proportional to P^(1/n). Therefore, comparing with P^x, we get x = 1/n.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I - Example of Colloids: (a) Cheese, (b) Pumice stone, (c) Hair cream, (d) Cloud. List II - Classification: (i) dispersion of liquid in liquid, (ii) dispersion of liquid in gas, (iii) dispersion of gas in solid, (iv) dispersion of liquid in solid. Choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below.
questions.sol_text: Matching colloids with their dispersed and dispersing medium phases: (1) Cheese - Liquid dispersed in Solid = dispersion of liquid in solid (iv); (2) Pumice stone - Gas dispersed in Solid = dispersion of gas in solid (iii); (3) Hair cream - Liquid dispersed in Liquid = dispersion of liquid in liquid (i); (4) Cloud - Liquid dispersed in Gas = dispersion of liquid in gas (ii). Therefore: (a) - (iv), (b) - (iii), (c) - (i), (d) - (ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Sodium stearate CH3(CH2)16COO Na+ is an anionic surfactant which forms micelles in oil. Choose the correct statement for it from the following:
options: It forms spherical micelles with CH3(CH2)16 - group pointing outwards on the surface of sphere.
It forms non-spherical micelles with -COO- group pointing outwards on the surface
It forms spherical micelles with CH3(CH2)16 - group pointing towards the centre of sphere.
It forms non-spherical micelles with CH3(CH2)16 - group pointing towards the centre.
questions.sol_text: In oil (non-polar solvent), sodium stearate forms reverse micelles. The ionic -COO Na+ (polar) head group points towards the center to minimize contact with oil, while the non-polar CH3(CH2)16 hydrocarbon tail points outwards towards the oil. This forms spherical micelles with the hydrocarbon part attracting and being repelled by the oil part. The correct answer is (A) - spherical micelles with CH3(CH2)16 group pointing outwards.

questions.sol_text: When FeCl3 is added to excess of hot water, hydrolysis occurs: FeCl3 + hydrolysis → Fe(OH)3↓ + Fe3+. The Fe(OH)3 colloidal particle absorbs Fe3+ ions (preferentially adsorbed ions from excess FeCl3), making the colloidal particles positively charged.

questions.text: Tyndall effect is more effectively shown by:
questions.sol_text: Tyndall effect is more effectively shown by lyophobic colloidal solution. The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles. It is more pronounced in lyophobic colloids because the particles are larger and have a greater tendency to scatter light compared to true solutions where particles are molecular in size. Lyophobic colloids have particles in the colloidal size range (1-1000 nm) that effectively scatter light.

The correct graph shows the T₁ isotherm positioned above the T₂ isotherm, indicating greater adsorption at the lower temperature. Graph (D) correctly displays this relationship with T₁ curve above T₂ curve.

questions.text: 100 ml of 0.0018% (w/v) solution of Cl ion was the minimum concentration of Cl required to precipitate a negative sol in one h. The coagulating value of Cl ion is _______. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol_text: Weight of Cl in 100 ml = 1.8 × 10^(-3) gm. Moles of Cl in 100 ml = (1.8 × 10^(-3))/35.5 = 0.0507 × 10^(-3) mole. Concentration [Cl^-] = (0.0507 × 10^(-3) × 1000)/100 = 5.07 × 10^(-3) M. This equals 0.507 milli mole in one litre required in one hour. Coagulation value = (milli mole/lit) required in one hr = 0.507 ≈ 1 (Nearest integer)

questions.text: 3.12 g of oxygen is adsorbed on 1.2 g of platinum metal. The volume oxygen adsorbed per gram of the adsorbent at 1 atm and 300 K in L is ________. [R = 0.0821 L atm K^(-1) mol^(-1)]
questions.sol_text: Using ideal gas law PV = nRT. First, find moles of O2: n = 3.12/32 = 0.0975 mol. Then, 1 × V = (3.12/32) × 0.0821 × 300, which gives V = 2.4 litres. Volume of O2 adsorbed per gram of adsorbent = 2.4 / 1.2 = 2 litres.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: CO2 gas adsorbs on charcoal following Freundlich adsorption isotherm. For a given amount of charcoal, the mass of CO2 adsorbed becomes 64 times when the pressure of CO2 is doubled. The value of n in the Freundlich isotherm equation is _____ × 10^-2. (Round off to the Nearest integer)
questions.sol_text: Using Freundlich isotherm equation: (x/m) = k(p)^(1/n). When pressure is doubled, mass adsorbed becomes 64 times. From equation (1): (x/m) = k(p)^(1/n). From equation (2): 64(x/m) = k(2p)^(1/n). Dividing equation (2) by equation (1): 64 = 2^(1/n). Taking logarithm: log(64) = (1/n)log(2). Since 64 = 2^6, we get: 6 = 1/n. Therefore: n = 1/6 = 0.167 = 16.7 × 10^-2. Rounded to nearest integer: 17 × 10^-2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Emulsion of oil in water are unstable and sometimes they separate into two layers on standing. Statement II: For stabilisation of an emulsion, excess of electrolyte is added. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol_text: Oil in water emulsions can sometimes separate into two layers on standing (e.g., milk). Therefore, Statement I is correct. On adding excess of electrolyte, coagulation occurs and emulsion is further destabilised. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For micelle formation, which of the following statements are correct? a. Micelle formation is an exothermic process. b. Micelle formation is an endothermic process. c. The entropy change is positive. d. The entropy change is negative.
questions.sol_text: Micelle formation is an endothermic process (b is correct) because it requires energy to disrupt the ordered structure of water molecules around the hydrophobic tails. The entropy change is positive (c is correct) because the ordered water molecules are released, increasing the disorder of the system. Therefore, both b and c are correct statements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), (B) CO(g) + 3H2(g) → CH4(g) + H2O(g), (C) CO(g) + H2(g) → HCHO(g), (D) CO(g) + 2H2(g) → CH3OH(g). List-II: (I) Cu, (II) Cu/ZnO − Cr2O3, (III) Fe3O4 + K2O + Al2O3, (IV) Ni. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.sol_text: Match each reaction with its correct catalyst: (A) N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g) uses catalyst Fe3O4 + K2O + Al2O3 (Haber's process), matched with (III). (B) CO(g) + 3H2(g) → CH4(g) + H2O(g) uses Ni catalyst (methanation), matched with (IV). (C) CO(g) + H2(g) → HCHO(g) uses Cu catalyst (formaldehyde synthesis), matched with (I). (D) CO(g) + 2H2(g) → CH3OH(g) uses Cu/ZnO − Cr2O3 catalyst (methanol synthesis), matched with (II). Therefore: (A)−(III), (B)−(IV), (C)−(I), (D)−(II).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Incorrect statement for Tyndall effect is:
options: The refractive indices of the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium differ greatly in magnitude.
The diameter of the dispersed particles is much smaller than the wavelength of the light used.
During projection of movies in the cinemas hall, Tyndall effect is noticed.
It is used to distinguish a true solution from a colloidal solution.
questions.sol_text: The Tyndall effect occurs when light is scattered by particles in a colloid. For the Tyndall effect to be observed, the diameter of the dispersed particles must be comparable to or not much smaller than the wavelength of light used (typically in the range of 40-900 nm). Statement (2) is incorrect because it states particles are much smaller than wavelength, which would not produce a visible Tyndall effect. Statements (1), (3), and (4) are all correct descriptions of the Tyndall effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Using very little soap while washing clothes, does not serve the purpose of cleaning of clothes, because:
options: soap particles remain floating in water as ions.
the hydrophobic part of soap is not able to take away grease.
the micelles are not formed due to concentration of soap, below its CMC value.
colloidal structure of soap in water is completely distributed.
questions.sol_text: When soap concentration is below the Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC), micelles cannot form. Micelles are necessary for effective cleaning as they trap dirt and grease particles. Without micelle formation, soap molecules remain as individual ions in water and cannot effectively remove grease from clothes. Therefore, very little soap (below CMC) does not serve the cleaning purpose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Finest gold is red in colour, as the size of the particles increases, it appears purple then blue and finally gold. Reason R: The colour of the colloidal solution depends on the wavelength of light scattered by the dispersed particles. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol_text: Finest gold sol is red in colour. As the size of colloidal particles increases, the wavelength of scattered light changes, causing the colour to appear purple, then blue, and finally golden. The colour of a colloidal solution depends on the wavelength of light scattered by the dispersed particles, which in turn depends on the size and nature of the particles. Therefore, both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Dissolved substances can be removed from a colloidal solution by diffusion through a parchment paper. Reason (R): Particles in a true solution cannot pass through parchment paper but the colloidal particles can pass through the parchment paper. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol_text: Parchment paper is a semi-permeable membrane which allows particles of true solution to pass through as their size is too small. Assertion is correct because dissolved substances (true solution particles) can pass through parchment paper by diffusion. However, Reason is incorrect because it states the opposite - that true solution particles cannot pass through parchment paper, which is false. In fact, colloidal particles cannot pass through parchment paper due to their larger size.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Activated charcoal adsorbs SO2 more efficiently than CH4. Reason R: Gases with lower critical temperatures are readily adsorbed by activated charcoal. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.sol_text: More polar gases easily adsorb on activated charcoal. And more polar gases have more (higher) critical temperature as compared to non-polar or less polar gases. Therefore, gases with higher critical temperature adsorbed more. This means Reason R is incorrect because it states lower critical temperatures are readily adsorbed. However, Assertion A is correct because SO2 is more polar than CH4, so SO2 adsorbs more efficiently than CH4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The Zeta potential is related to which property of colloids?
options: Charge on the surface of colloidal particles
questions.sol_text: The zeta potential is the potential difference between the fixed layer and the diffused layer of opposite charges around a colloidal particle. It is directly related to the charge on the surface of colloidal particles. The magnitude of zeta potential determines the stability of the colloidal dispersion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 100 mL of 5% (w/v) solution of NaCl in water was prepared in 250 mL beaker. Albumin from the egg was poured into NaCl solution and stirred well. This resulted in a/an:
questions.sol_text: Standard method for the preparation of lyophilic sol. When albumin (a protein) is added to NaCl solution and stirred well, it dissolves to form a lyophilic sol. Albumin is a hydrophilic protein that readily disperses in aqueous salt solutions to form a true lyophilic colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is a correct statement?
options: Any amount of dispersed phase can be added to emulsion without destabilising it.
Mixing two oppositely charged sols in equal amount neutralises charges and stabilises colloids.
Presence of equal and similar charges on colloidal particles provides stability to the colloidal solution.
questions.sol_text: Statement (4) is correct. The stability of colloidal solutions is due to the presence of equal and similar charges on colloidal particles. These charges create electrostatic repulsion between particles, preventing their aggregation. Statement (1) is wrong - Brownian motion actually keeps sols stable by preventing settling. Statement (2) is wrong - adding excess dispersed phase destabilises emulsions. Statement (3) is wrong - neutralising charges leads to destabilisation and precipitation, not stabilisation.

questions.text: 2.0 g of H2 gas is adsorbed on 2.5 g of platinum powder at 300 K and 1 bar pressure. The volume of the gas adsorbed per gram of the adsorbent is _____ mL. (Given: R = 0.083 L bar K^(-1) mol^(-1))
questions.sol_text: Using ideal gas law PV = nRT. First find moles of H2: n = 2.0/2 = 1 mol. Calculate volume: V = nRT/P = (1 × 0.083 × 300)/(1) = 24.9 litre. Convert to mL: 24.9 L = 24900 mL. Volume per gram of adsorbent = 24900/2.5 = 9960 mL
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: If the initial pressure of a gas 0.03 atm, the mass of the gas absorbed per gram of the adsorbent is ____ × 10^(-2) g.
questions.sol_text: From the graph, intercept = 0.602 = log 4, so K = 4. Slope = 1/n = 1, so n = 1. Using the Freundlich adsorption equation: x/m = K(p)^(1/n) = 4 × (0.03)^1 = 4 × 0.03 = 0.12 = 12 × 10^(-2). Therefore, mass of gas absorbed per gram of adsorbent = 12 × 10^(-2) g.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Among the following the number of curves not in accordance with Freundlich adsorption isotherm is ______.
questions.sol_text: The Freundlich adsorption isotherm equation is: log(x/m) = log k + (1/n)log P, where x/m is the amount of adsorbate per unit mass of adsorbent and P is the pressure. When plotted as log(x/m) vs log P, it gives a straight line. Analyzing the curves: (a) Shows curved plot of log(x/m) vs log P - NOT Freundlich (should be linear on log-log plot). (b) Shows linear plot of log(x/m) vs P - NOT Freundlich (should be log-log, not semi-log). (c) Shows linear plot of log(x/m) vs P - NOT Freundlich (should be log-log, not semi-log). (D) Shows linear plot of log(x/m) vs log P - This IS Freundlich isotherm (correct). Therefore, 3 curves (a, b, and c) are not in accordance with Freundlich adsorption isotherm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: When 200 mL of 0.2 M acetic acid is shaken with 0.6 g of wood charcoal, the final concentration of acetic acid after adsorption is 0.1 M. The mass of acetic acid adsorbed per gram of carbon is _______ g.
questions.sol_text: Mass of wood charcoal = 0.6 g. Initial moles of acetic acid = 0.2 × 0.2 = 0.04 mol. Final moles of acetic acid = 0.1 × 0.2 = 0.02 mol. Moles of acetic acid adsorbed = 0.04 - 0.02 = 0.02 mol. Mass of acetic acid adsorbed = 0.02 × 60 = 1.2 g. Mass of acetic acid adsorbed per gram of charcoal = 1.2 / 0.6 = 2.0 g.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following represents the Freundlich adsorption isotherms?
questions.sol_text: The Freundlich adsorption isotherm equation is x/m = KP^(1/n), which can be written as log(x/m) = logK + (1/n)logP. This is a linear equation when log(x/m) is plotted against logP with slope 1/n and intercept logK. Therefore: (A) x/m vs p shows curved behavior matching the non-linear form (correct), (B) log(x/m) vs log p shows linear behavior matching equation (ii) (correct), (C) x/m vs c shows linear behavior but 'c' is not the correct variable (incorrect), (D) x/m vs p^(1/n) shows linear behavior which matches the original equation rearranged (correct). Thus A, B, D are correct representations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The enthalpy change for the adsorption process and micelle formation respectively are.
questions.sol_text: The adsorption process is exothermic, so ΔH_ads < 0 (negative). For micelle formation, the process is driven by entropy increase (ΔS is positive), and for spontaneity at room temperature, ΔH_mic must be > 0 (positive, endothermic). This is consistent with the hydrophobic effect where micelle formation is entropy-driven rather than enthalpy-driven.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: A. Osmosis, B. Reverse osmosis, C. Electro osmosis, D. Electrophoresis. List-II: I. Solvent molecules pass through semi permeable membrane towards solvent side. II. Movement of charged colloidal particles under the influence of applied electric potential towards oppositely charged electrodes. III. Solvent molecules pass through semi permeable membrane towards solution side. IV. Dispersion medium moves in an electric field.
questions.sol_text:
Correct match is:
A. Osmosis - III. Solvent molecules pass through semi permeable membrane towards solution side.
B. Reverse osmosis - I. Solvent molecules pass to solvent side through SPM.
C. Electro osmosis - IV. Dispersion medium moves in an electric field.
D. Electrophoresis - II. Movement of colloidal particle towards oppositely charged electrodes.

Osmosis is the movement of solvent molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from the region of higher solvent concentration (lower solute concentration) to the region of lower solvent concentration (higher solute concentration), which corresponds to movement towards the solution side.

Reverse osmosis is the opposite process where solvent molecules pass through a semi-permeable membrane from the solution side to the solvent side when external pressure is applied.

Electro osmosis is the movement of the dispersion medium (solvent) in an electric field, not the solute particles.

Electrophoresis is the movement of charged colloidal particles through a medium under the influence of an applied electric field towards the oppositely charged electrode.

Therefore the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Adding surfactants in non polar solvent, the micelles structure will look like
options: Non Polar Solvent with polar heads pointing inward and non-polar tails pointing outward
Non Polar Solvent with mixed arrangement of surfactant molecules
Non Polar Solvent with non-polar tails pointing inward and polar heads pointing outward
Non Polar Solvent with densely packed surfactant molecules in organized arrangement
questions.sol_text:
In a non-polar solvent, the behavior of surfactants is opposite to that in polar solvents (like water).

Surfactant structure: Polar head - non-polar tail

In non-polar solvents:
- The non-polar part (tail) will interact favorably with the non-polar solvent
- The polar part (head) will try to minimize contact with the non-polar solvent
- Therefore, the polar heads will point INWARD (toward the center) and the non-polar tails will point OUTWARD (toward the solvent)

This creates a REVERSE MICELLE structure, where:
- Polar heads cluster together in the center
- Non-polar tails extend outward into the non-polar solvent

Looking at the options:
(a) Shows polar heads pointing inward with non-polar tails pointing outward - this is the reverse micelle structure
(b) Shows a more dispersed arrangement
(c) Shows non-polar tails pointing inward (incorrect - opposite of what happens)
(d) Shows a dense organized packing

Option (a) correctly represents the reverse micelle formation in non-polar solvents.

Matching with the numbered options:
(1) c - incorrect structure
(2) a - CORRECT (reverse micelle with heads inward)
(3) d - incorrect structure
(4) b - incorrect structure

Therefore, the answer is (2) which corresponds to option (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The graph of log(x/m) vs log p for an adsorption process is a straight line inclined at an angle of 45° with intercept equal to 0.6020. The mass of gas adsorbed per unit mass of adsorbent at the pressure of 0.4 atm is _______ × 10^(-1) (Nearest integer). Given: log 2 = 0.3010
questions.sol_text:
Given: The graph of log(x/m) vs log p is a straight line inclined at 45° with intercept 0.6020.

For a straight line: log(x/m) = (slope) × log p + intercept

Slope = tan(45°) = 1

Intercept = log k = 0.6020
Therefore, k = 10^(0.6020) = 4

The equation becomes: log(x/m) = 1 × log p + log k
log(x/m) = log p + log k
log(x/m) = log(k.p)

Therefore: x/m = k.p^(1/n) where n = 1 (from slope = 1/n)

At p = 0.4 atm:
x/m = k × p^1 = 4 × 0.4 = 1.6 g

Expressing as requested: 1.6 × 10^(-1) g

Nearest integer: 16.00 (where the answer is 16.00 × 10^(-1) = 1.6 g)
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
